{{short description|German mathematician}}
[[File:Otto Haupt 4.jpeg|thumb|upright|Otto Haupt.]]
'''Otto Haupt'''  (born 5 March 1887 in [[Würzburg]]; died 10 November 1988 in [[Bad Soden]]) was a German mathematician.

==Biography==
Haupt obtained his PhD in 1911 under the supervision of [[Georg Rost]] and [[Emil Hilb]] at the [[University of Würzburg]],<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=46735}}</ref> and became a professor at the [[University of Erlangen-Nuremberg]]. He retired from teaching in 1953, but continued his mathematical research for many subsequent years.<ref name="jacobs">{{citation|title=Otto Haupt: Centenarian mathematician|first=Konrad|last=Jacobs|journal=[[The Mathematical Intelligencer]]|volume=9|issue=4|pages=50–51|doi=10.1007/BF03023732|year=1987|s2cid=123140526}}.</ref>

Since 1918 he was married to Edith Hughes. Despite her Jewish ancestry, she survived the Nazi period unharmed in Erlangen, and lived to 1981.<ref name="jacobs"/>

==Research and publications==
Haupt specialized in [[geometry]] and [[real analysis]]; many of his research publications related to the [[four-vertex theorem]] on local minima and maxima of curvature. He also wrote textbooks on [[algebra]] and [[calculus]].<ref name="jacobs"/>

==Awards and honors==
In 1987, his centenary year, a birthday conference was given in his honor at the University of Erlangen.<ref name="jacobs"/><ref name="bauer">{{citation|language=German|title=Otto Haupt — Zum 100. Geburtstag|first=Heinz|last=Bauer|journal=[[Aequationes Mathematicae]]|volume=32|issue=1|pages=1–5|doi=10.1007/BF02311293|year=1987|s2cid=123128849}}.</ref>

He was awarded honorary doctorates from the [[University of Bonn]], the [[University of Nantes]] and the [[University of Würzburg]].<ref name="jacobs"/><ref name="bauer"/><ref>Jahrbuch der Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, 1988, p. 236: "Haupt war Ehrendoktor der Universitäten Bonn, Würzburg und Nantes".</ref>
